newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Nestle 1st-half profit jumps but shares slip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nestle 1st-half profit jumps but shares slip.

text.p: Nestle SA, the world's biggest foods and beverage company, said net profit rose 20 percent in the first half of 1996, but its share price fell on Friday as investors focused instead on stagnant trading results.
Group net profit swelled by a fifth compared with the year-earlier period to 1.35 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion), the company said in its interim report from Vevey, on the shores of Lake Geneva.

This was roughly in line with analysts' forecasts, but dealers seized on barely changed trading profits and Nestle's forecast that profit growth would slow in the second half of the year as reasons to mark prices down.
Shares opened at 1,417 Swiss francs, down from the previous close at 1,423, and slipped briefly below 1,400 at midday.

"I will keep my neutral rating (for Nestle) relative to the Swiss market, but in the short term prices will continue to come under pressure," said James Amoroso, an analyst for CS Investment Research in Zurich.

He pointed to first-half trading profits that rose less than one percent from the year-earlier period to 2.46 billion francs. Its trading margin, which measures trading profit against sales, slipped to 8.6 percent from 9.1 percent in 1995.
"People were looking for a 9.7 margin and we got 8.6, which was very disappointing," Amoroso said.
Analyst Rene Weber at Bank Vontobel in Zurich said the marginal rise in trading profit was a "negative surprise".

"On the basis of this I think a lot of analysts will be revising their estimates for the whole year," he said, adding he had marked projected earnings per share down to 82 francs from his earlier estimate of 84.50.
"These numbers were slightly disappointing, but Nestle remains attractive by international comparison," Weber added.
Nestle said first half sales rose 5.6 percent to 28.44 billion francs, boosted primarily by internal sales growth. Currency fluctuations had a slight negative effect on turnover.

"For the full year 1996, Nestle expects the favourable trend in sales to continue, and consolidated sales for the year should approach 60 billion Swiss francs," it said. Its 1995 sales totalled 56.48 billion Swiss francs.
But it added net profits would not rise as fast in the second half because the first half rate was based in part on comparison with a feeble start to 1995.

"The net profit growth rate registered during the first six months of the year will not be sustained over the second semester, as its very favourable evolution is due to the comparison with a rather weak period during the first six months of 1995," it explained.
"For the whole of 1996, net profit should grow at least at the same rate as consolidated sales," it added, but it did not give a precise estimate for 1996 profit.

Nestle said the cost of goods sold dipped as a percentage of sales in the first half, but this was offset by increased marketing expenses to boost the group's brands as well as higher restructuring and amortisation costs.
Nestle posted a 1995 group net profit of 2.92 billion francs, down from 3.25 billion in 1994, when sales of cosmetics businesses produced an exceptional gain of 306 million francs.
Nestle said sales volume rose 3.6 percent in the first half of 1996 excluding acquisitions and disinvestments, compared with around three percent in the same period of 1995. ($1=1.2392 Swiss Franc)
